## High Level Overview of Change

This branch resolves #3932. The concept of "fee units" has been (almost) completely removed. It remains in a few places to preserve backward compatibility. Additionally, a new amendment, `XRPFees` has been introduced which, if enabled by the validators, will convert all representations of fees in the code, ledger, and protocol that are still raw numbers into `XRPAmount`s.

issues.title: No protocol-enforced ceiling on base fee post-XRPFees amendment
issues.author: mvadari
issues.body:
The XRPFees amendment removed the internal data-type-based ceiling on the base fee. Validators can now vote the base fee to any valid XRP amount via the median-vote fee-voting mechanism on flag ledgers (\~every 15 minutes). There is no protocol-enforced upper bound. The report frames this as part of a structural exploit chain enabling "silent XRP drainage via validator-coordinated fee manipulation" that is "nearly impossible to prove as intentional."

issues.author: intelliot
issues.body:
## Issue Description
https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/pull/4247 introduces an amendment, `featureXRPFees` (`XRPFees` for short), and causes some breaking API changes.

The motivations for the amendment:
- The fee code is unnecessarily complex due to arcane concepts like "fee units" and "reference transactions" - represented as integers of various widths. A lot of effort is expended to keep all that straight and prevent developers from doing the wrong thing.
- Fee units are hard-coded to 10 and the "reference transaction" fee is also 10, so there is an opportunity to reduce complexity: replace "fee units" with `XRPAmount` for all fees. Scaling/adjusting of fees can operate directly on `XRPAmo
